sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:238265
Court No. - 76

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 46461 of 2023
Applicant :- Suhail Khan

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ambreen Masroor,Sadrul Islam Jafri,Sr. Advocate
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Manish Trivedi
Hon'ble Vikram D. Chauhan,J.
1.
Learned A.G.A. for the State submits that instructions have been received and has no objection in case the bail application is heard on merits.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Manish Trivedi, learned counsel for the ICICI,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant was not named in the First Information Report and the FIR was lodged with the allegation that Kanpur Electricity Supply Company had opened a current account in the Bank and through payment gateway, customers were depositing the payment against the electricity bill dues.
The aforesaid Company made a complaint to the Bank that the amount is not being transferred in the account of the Company and a sum of Rs.1,48,20,273/- is alleged to have been siphoned off.
The amount was transferred in the account of one Company in the name of KESCO Electronic, of which proprietor is co-accused Suman.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that no amount has been transferred in the account of applicant from the account of KESCO Electronics.

The amount has been transferred in the Suhail Khan vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189067038/
1 account of 27 accused persons, however, no amount has been transferred in favour of the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the name of applicant has surfaced on account of fact that applicant was apprehended by the police along with Rs.45,00,000/- after 12 days from the car on the basis of information given by mukhbir-khas.
It is submitted that there is no material evidence to the complicity of applicant in the present case.
It is submitted that mere recovery of Rs.45,00,000/- by itself cannot be presumed that the aforesaid amount is connected with the present case.
There is no evidence in the present case to link the recovery of Rs.45,00,000/- with the present crime.
The criminal history of the applicant has been explained in paragraph no.43 of the affidavit, in which the applicant has already been acquitted.
Applicant is languishing in jail since 8.8.2023 and in case he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the trial.

4. Learned counsel for the ICICI has opposed the bail application and submits that from the account of applicant a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- has been transferred on 22.6.2023 in the account of co-accused Kundan Kumar.

The aforesaid transaction being made in the account of co-accused, as such,
applicant is also liable.

5. Learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail and submits that as per prosecution case,
Rs.45,00,000/- has been recovered from the applicant after 12 days from the car and the applicant made complicity in the present case on the basis of confessional statement.
6.
Learned AGA for the State has pointed out the criminal antecedents of the applicant.
No material or circumstance has been brought to the notice of this Court with regard to tampering of evidence or intimidating of witness in previous criminal cases.
In Ash Mohammad Vs. Shiv Raj Singh, (2012) 9 SCC 446, the Apex Court in para 30 has observed:-

entities.text: Ash Mohammad Vs. Shiv Raj Singh, (2012) 9 SCC 446
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "We may hasten to add that when we state that the accused is a history-sheeter we may not be understood to have said that a history-sheeter is never entitled to bail.

But, it is a significant factor to be taken note of regard being had to the nature of crime in respect of which he has been booked."
7.

In the case of Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2020 (11) SCC 648, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused may itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2020 (11) SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In so far as criminal antecedents of the applicant is concerned, it is not the case of the State that applicant might tamper with or otherwise adversely influence the investigation, or that he might intimidate witnesses before or during the trial.
The State has also not placed any material that applicant in past attempted to evade the process of law.

If the accused is otherwise found to be entitled to bail, he cannot be denied bail only on the ground of criminal history, no exceptional circumstances on the basis of criminal antecedents have been shown to deny bail to accused, hence,
the Court does not feel it proper to deny bail to the applicant just on the ground that he had criminal antecedent.

2 9.

sentences.text: The principle that Bail is a rule and Jail is an exception has been well recognised by Apex Court more specifically on the touch stone of Article 21 of the Constitution.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Apex Court in Satyendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51.

entities.text: Satyendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA has not shown any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.

10. No material, facts or circumstances has been shown by learned AGA for the State that the accused may tamper with the evidence or witnesses or the accused is of such character that his mere presence at large would intimidate the witnesses or that accused will use his liberty to subvert justice or tamper with the evidence.
11. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA for the State.
12. Learned AGA for the State has not shown any material or circumstances that the accused/applicant is not entitled to bail in larger interests of the public or State.
13. It is to be seen in the present case that from the account of the aforesaid Company payment made by customers siphoned off in the account of account of co-accused.
From the account of co-accused, amount has been transferred in the account of 27 other accused persons.
No amount has been transferred in the account of applicant.

Since a sum of Rs.45,00,000/- is alleged to have been recovered from the applicant after 12 days from the car, however, there is no linking evidence that the amount so recovered is connected with the present crime, has been shown by the prosecution.

14. Learned counsel for the Bank has drawn attention of this Court to the fact that a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- has been transferred by the applicant in the account of co-accused, who was the software engineer, however, the aforesaid fact only brings suspicion but cannot be a ground to proceed against applicant at this stage.
Since no linking evidence shown, a person cannot be permitted to remain in jail only on the ground of suspicion unless there is material evidence.

15. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant Suhail Khan involved in Case Crime No.207 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420,
409, 120-B IPC and Section 66(D) Information Technology Act, Police Station Kotwali, District Kanpur Nagar be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions:-
i.
The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.

Suhail Khan vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189067038/
3 ii.

entities.text: Suhail Khan vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.

iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted and/or the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.
iv.
The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
vi. The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court.
vii. In the event, the applicant changes residential address, the applicant shall inform the court concerned about new residential address in writing.
17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
